verbatim: Every morning it posts a wall of text, I stopped opening it.
what_happened: The project bot posted a 40-line status thread in every project channel each morning; none got a human reply in two weeks.

countermeasures.text: Prompt asks for a short status, five lines at most.

check.how: Read the next 10 morning posts and count the human replies.

log.text: to_check -> recurred: the cause came back (A002)

verbatim: Still too long, and it says the same thing every day.
what_happened: Posts went back to 25 to 40 lines within a week; the five-line instruction was ignored on busy projects.
wrong_assumption: A model will keep to a length written in its prompt.

countermeasures.text: The bot now speaks only when something changed since yesterday: a one-line card in the channel, the details in a thread under it. The daily digest is gone.

log.text: countermeasure mechanism: The bot now speaks only when something changed since yesterday: a one-line card in the channel, the details in a thread under it. The daily digest is gone.

check.how: Count bot posts and posts with a human reply over two weeks, against 61 posts and 0 replies before.
check.proof: Two weeks counted: 9 posts instead of 61, 6 with a human reply.

elsewhere: Checked the sales coach and the weekly digest for the same pattern.

reply.text: You were right, it talked every day even when nothing had moved, so now it only speaks when something changed, in one line, with the details in a thread if you want them; if you see it rambling again, tell me.

verbatim: It drafted a follow-up to the buyer who asked us last month to stop writing.
what_happened: The outreach agent drafted a follow-up email to a buyer at an industrial client who had asked not to be contacted; the sales rep caught it before sending.
wrong_assumption: The do-not-contact list lives in the CRM, so the agent will see it.
earlier: At draft time, by checking the recipient against the list in code.

countermeasures.text: Every recipient is checked in code against the do-not-contact list before a draft is created; a blocked draft is never stored, and the agent is told why.

check.how: Count drafts since the fix and how many the list blocked; zero drafts to a listed person.
check.proof: 42 drafts since Oct 6, 3 blocked by the list, 0 addressed to a listed person; the original case is in the test suite.

verbatim: It says we are 116 days late on a delivery we did in September.
what_happened: The cockpit flagged a client delivery as 116 days late; it happened on time, but the date field in the project base was never updated.
wrong_assumption: Someone updates the delivery date by hand after the meeting.

countermeasures.text: The delivery date is read from the calendar event of the delivery meeting, no longer typed by hand.

waiting_for: Review and merge of the PR that reads dates from the calendar.

verbatim: You told me it was done and the page was blank.
what_happened: Claude reported a change as working after a green typecheck; the page crashed on load.
wrong_assumption: A green typecheck means the page works.

countermeasures.text: Global CLAUDE.md, rule 1: done means seen working (run it, see the effect).
End-of-turn hook reruns the project checks from verify.json and sends Claude back to work when they fail.

check.how: Over two weeks, count the times the CEO found a broken change after hearing done, and the blocks in the hook log.
